newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Gaelic Games-Mayo bids to revive glory days.
newsitem.headline: Gaelic Games-Mayo bids to revive glory days.

text.p: Connacht champions Mayo will bid to revive memories of the glory days in the West of Ireland when they meet Leinster champions Meath in the All-Ireland football final at Croke Park on Sunday.
It is 30 years since a Connacht side last won the All-Ireland, while Mayo won the last of their three football titles in 1951 when they beat Meath in the final.
"I don't know if you could justify the bad press Mayo have received over the years although I suppose there was good reason for it a couple of times," team manager John Maughan said.
Never more so than after Mayo's 20-point defeat by Cork in the 1993 All-Ireland semi-final when they lost by 5-15 (30) to 0-10 (10), .
"John Maughan has really drilled it into us that no Mayo team must ever be humiliated again," said Anthony Finnerty, who played in the 1993 game but will be a substitute on Sunday.

"Believe me, we'd risk our limbs to go out and play in the red and green jersey. We're that bonded now. We're not ever going to be humiliated like that again. As long as I play football, I'll never be humiliated like that," he added.
Mayo last contested an All-Ireland final in 1989 when they were beaten by Cork on a scoreline of 0-17 (17) to 1-11 (14).
This year Mayo beat London, a team mostly made up of ex-patriots, Roscommon and Galway to lift the Connacht title.
Mayo then beat the well-fancied Munster champions Kerry in the All-Ireland semi-final.
The Connacht champions have made one change to the team which beat Kerry for Sunday's final. David Brady has returned to the squad after injury and he replaces Pat Fallon at midfield.
Defender Dermot Flanagan and midfielder Liam McHale are the only two survivors from the Mayo side beaten in the 1989 final.
Opponents Meath won the last of their five All-Ireland football titles in 1988.
Defenders Colm Coyle and Martin O'Connell are the only two players on the team for Sunday who were also involved when Cork were beaten in the replayed 1988 decider.
The Meathmen had to beat Carlow, Laois and champions Dublin before they lifted the Leinster title this year. They then beat Ulster champions Tyrone in the All-Ireland semi-final.
Meath have made no changes to the team which beat Tyrone for Sunday's final.
Midfielder Jimmy McGuinness has been passed fit to play after undergoing a late fitness test for a leg injury he picked up in an accidental collision with a team-mate at training during the week.

MAYO: 1-John Madden; 2-Kenneth Mortimer, 3-Kevin Cahill, 4-Dermot Flanagan; 5-Pat Holmes, 6-James Nallen, 7-Noel Connelly (Captain); 8-Liam McHale, 9-David Brady; 10-James Horan, 11-Colm McMenamon, 12-Maurice Sheridan; 13-David Nestor, 14-John Casey, 15-Ray Dempsey.

MEATH: 1-Conor Martin; 2-Mark O'Reilly, 3-Darren Fay, 4-Martin O'Connell; 5-Colm Coyle, 6-Enda McManus, 7-Paddy Reynolds; 8-Jimmy McGuinness, 9-John McDermott; 10-Terry Giles, 11- Tommy Dowd (Captain), 12-Graham Geraghty; 13-Evan Kelly, 14-Brendan Reilly, 15-Barry Callaghan.
